anomalies.description: Organic carbon of 0.64 g/kg is critically depleted; soil food web and moisture retention have collapsed, making plant establishment for pollinators extremely difficult.
anomalies.recommended_action: Apply 5 t/ha of well-rotted farmyard manure or biochar immediately; plant a mixed legume-grass cover crop and leave undisturbed for 18 months.

anomalies.description: Drought index of 1.00 (scale 0–1) indicates severe moisture deficit; evapotranspiration is drastically exceeding rainfall over the past 30 days.
anomalies.recommended_action: Activate all available irrigation systems on pollinator habitat areas; report drought conditions to the District Agriculture Officer / KVK for emergency support.

anomalies.description: Rainfall of 13.7 mm over 30 days is 16.3 mm below the recommended minimum – expect reduced nectar concentration.
anomalies.recommended_action: Check field-margin flowering plant health weekly; prepare drip-irrigation lines for wildflower strips and activate if the 7-day forecast shows less than 10 mm.

anomalies.description: Pollinator visitation is reduced to 64% of expected activity (18.8 vs 29.2 visits/hour).
anomalies.recommended_action: Add staggered flowering strips beside the crop edge and pause non-essential sprays during bloom.

anomalies.description: Flowering success is 46%, below the expected level for a stable crop cycle.
anomalies.recommended_action: Survey flower-to-fruit set across representative rows and add supplemental forage near low-performing rows.

biodiversity_insight: Soil fertility loss is the primary threat here, severely depleting organic carbon and collapsing the soil food web, which will cut crop yields by an estimated 20-30% this season.
top_intervention: Apply 5 tons per hectare of organic compost during the next pre-monsoon season to restore soil health and support pollinators.

anomalies.description: Pesticide concentration of 15.0 ppm is critically high and likely lethal to bees on contact.
anomalies.recommended_action: Immediately suspend all pyrethroid applications; switch to a Bee Hazard Class II-rated alternative and allow a minimum 21-day clearance period before next application.

anomalies.description: 7 applications per month far exceeds safe practice and creates chronic sub-lethal exposure that impairs bee navigation and queen fertility.
anomalies.recommended_action: Adopt an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) protocol limiting applications to ≤2 per month and introduce biological controls (e.g. Trichogramma wasps, chrysopids) as a buffer.
